title: CmdPal: Extension SDK 0.12.260812002 can't be used with project using old .NET versions
author: jiripolasek
summary: The CmdPal SDK package likely ships a net10-built toolkit assembly under net8 NuGet metadata, forcing .NET 10 on older extension projects.

judgment.rationale: The issue is engineering-owned and source evidence shows a credible mismatch: the SDK nuspec advertises net8 assets while the toolkit project inherits the repo-wide net10 target after the .NET 10 upgrade.
evidence: The report identifies SDK 0.12.260812002 forcing .NET 10 onto older extension projects.
The author is a collaborator and removed the generic Needs-Author-Feedback label after the bot request.
src/modules/cmdpal/extensionsdk/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit.csproj imports the common target and has no explicit package TFM override.
src/modules/cmdpal/extensionsdk/nuget/Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.SDK.nuspec declares net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0 dependencies and copies the toolkit DLL into lib/net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the fork-side implementation design that aligns the built toolkit assembly, nuspec metadata, and packaging verification.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete upstream or fork implementation is present. The existing design targets the apparent package TFM mismatch and adds a packaging guard, but the published package payload still needs direct inspection before implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Align the CmdPal SDK toolkit target framework with its NuGet assets
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The toolkit project inherits the repository net10 target while the SDK nuspec places its managed assembly and dependency group under net8, allowing a net10-built payload to be advertised as net8-compatible.
plan: Set an explicit SDK toolkit target framework matching the package lib and dependency-group TFM, preserving CsWinRT and native runtime asset behavior.
Add a terminating BuildSDKHelper.ps1 pre-pack check that compares the toolkit assembly/deps target framework with the nuspec asset folder.
Build a minimal net8 extension consumer against the generated package and keep the existing net10 template build covered.
verification: Inspect the generated nupkg to confirm the toolkit assembly metadata, deps runtime target, nuspec dependency group, and lib folder all agree.
Restore and build a minimal net8 Windows consumer from the local package source without requiring .NET 10.

confidence.rationale: The repository target and nuspec mismatch are directly observed and fit the report, but the exact published package payload must be confirmed before choosing the final target framework.

issue_context.summary: A Command Palette Extension SDK package version associated with PowerToys 0.101 is not usable by older .NET extension projects because the package appears to introduce .NET 10 requirements despite net8 package metadata.
known_information: The report targets Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions SDK version 0.12.260812002 and PowerToys 0.101.
The report concerns NuGet package consumption by extension projects, not PowerToys runtime behavior.
The extension template now targets net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0.
No assignee, linked fix, or duplicate is present.
inferences: The package probably contains a net10-built toolkit assembly or deps payload under net8 metadata; implementation must confirm this against the produced nupkg.
issue_context.analysis: The missing detail is not reporter-side repro data; it is package build output verification. The design therefore targets SDK build/pack alignment and adds a package compatibility gate.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, bot comment, label timeline, current labels/assignees, and duplicate search results.

Inspected Common.Dotnet.props, Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit.csproj, Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.SDK.nuspec, BuildSDKHelper.ps1, the extension template csproj, and solution membership.
Checked recent history and found the .NET 10 upgrade commit in the affected file history.
Created fork mirror issue for the converged design after confirming no existing [Issue 50235] fork issue existed.

information_gaps.information: The actual lib assembly TargetFrameworkAttribute and deps runtimeTarget from SDK version 0.12.260812002
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes the suspected net10 payload mismatch from a different package dependency or restore cause before implementation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Inspect the published nupkg contents and assembly/deps metadata, then repeat with the locally generated package.

design.root_cause: The SDK package advertises its managed toolkit under lib/net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0, but the toolkit project inherits the repo-wide net10.0 target from Common.Dotnet.props. After the .NET 10 upgrade, the DLL and deps.json copied into the net8 package folder can be built for .NET 10, so older extension projects restore a package that looks net8-compatible but receives net10 assets.
evidence: Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.Toolkit.csproj imports Common.Dotnet.CsWinRT.props and does not override TargetFramework for SDK packaging.
Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.SDK.nuspec declares a net8 dependency group and lib/net8 file targets.
BuildSDKHelper.ps1 builds the toolkit and then packs the nuspec without checking assembly/deps target frameworks.
The template targets net10, so template builds no longer catch older consumer compatibility.

affected_files.purpose: Managed toolkit assembly target framework and CsWinRT build inputs.
NuGet dependency group and lib folder contract.
SDK build and pack pipeline where package asset TFMs can be validated.
First-party template and consumer smoke reference point.
Existing test project to pair with focused packaging compatibility checks.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The toolkit inherits net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0 from the shared repo props while being packaged under a net8 lib folder.
implementation_steps.change: Introduce an explicit SDK packaging TFM such as CmdPalSdkTargetFramework defaulting to net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0, or deliberately retarget both package metadata and consumers to net10 if maintainers choose to drop older support. Preferred fix is to build the toolkit for the same TFM the package exposes.
edge_cases: Keep CsWinRT input paths and native winmd/DLL copy behavior intact.
Verify APIs used by the toolkit are available when compiling for net8.
Do not change COM server or MSIX hosting patterns for extensions.
tests: Inspect the built DLL TargetFrameworkAttribute and deps.json runtimeTarget.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The script packs whatever toolkit DLL/deps files exist into the net8 package folder without verifying their target framework.
implementation_steps.change: Add a pre-pack verification step that reads the toolkit deps.json and/or assembly metadata and throws if it does not match the nuspec lib folder TFM.
edge_cases: Use terminating errors so CI fails before publishing a bad package.
Validate the AnyCPU toolkit payload once while still building both native architectures.
tests: Temporarily force a mismatch and confirm the script fails before nuget pack.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The nuspec unconditionally declares net8 metadata even if the actual DLL was built for net10.
implementation_steps.change: Keep the net8 dependency group and lib folder only if the DLL is actually built for net8; otherwise retarget dependency group and lib folder to net10 together and document the breaking change. Do not ship mixed metadata.
edge_cases: Avoid multiple lib groups unless separate builds produce matching DLLs.
Keep native runtime assets under runtimes/win-x64 and runtimes/win-arm64.
tests: Open the generated nupkg and assert lib folder, deps runtimeTarget, and assembly TargetFrameworkAttribute agree.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The official template targets net10, so it validates recommended modern extension creation but not older package consumption.
implementation_steps.change: Add a package smoke validation path using a minimal net8 extension consumer that references the freshly built local nupkg; keep the template on net10 unless maintainers choose a broader template support change.
implementation_steps.code_block:
dotnet new console -f net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0
dotnet add package Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions --source <local _build>
dotnet build /p:EnableMsixTooling=false
edge_cases: The smoke test should not require deploy, COM registration, or MSIX packaging.
If net8 support is dropped intentionally, update docs and expected smoke target instead.
tests: Restore/build the minimal net8 consumer against the local nupkg.
Build the existing net10 template to ensure recommended usage still works.

verify: Inspect src\modules\cmdpal\extensionsdk\_build\Microsoft.CommandPalette.Extensions.*.nupkg and confirm the toolkit DLL TargetFrameworkAttribute and deps runtimeTarget match the nuspec lib folder.
Create a minimal net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0 consumer against the local package source and confirm restore/build does not require .NET 10.
Build the existing net10 TemplateCmdPalExtension project to confirm the recommended template still works.
risks: Building toolkit for net8 may reveal APIs or dependencies introduced only for net10.
CsWinRT/native winmd packaging is architecture-sensitive; preserve x64 and arm64 native assets.
Changing package metadata to net10 instead would be a breaking support decision, not just a bug fix.
alternatives: Only changing the nuspec folder to net10 was rejected because it would make the package honest but would not restore older-project compatibility.
Only changing the template was rejected because existing consumers still fail.
Adding no verification was rejected because a future repo-wide TFM change could silently reintroduce the mismatch.

non_blocking_notes: Confirm the exact published 0.12.260812002 nupkg TFM before implementation; if it came from a different branch, the same design applies as a packaging-pipeline verification fix.
